function: Excluded, no_learning (p. 10): cascaded IRS channel estimation in cell-free mMIMO-OTFS by ConvBL, an iterative EM sparse Bayesian learning algorithm run per pilot observation; no trained model.
notes: PDF matches the DOI: p. 1 holds the title 'IRS-Enhanced Cell-Free mMIMO-OTFS Systems: Learning-Based Channel Estimator and SE Analysis' and DOI 10.1109/TWC.2025.3595411. Reason no_learning, shown on p. 10: the physical-layer function (uplink cascaded UE-IRS-AP delay-Doppler channel estimation) is performed by ConvBL, a sparse Bayesian learning algorithm, which is an iterative EM algorithm without trained parameters. p. 10: 'Our ConvBL algorithm integrates the system-specific prior discussed in Sec. V-A into an iterative Bayesian learning framework.' p. 10: 'directly optimizing the parameter estimates based on the observed data'. p. 1: 'employs expectation-maximization (EM) procedure to calculate the channel posterior distribution in the E step, and natural gradient descent algorithm to calculate the prior parameters in the M step'. p. 11, Algorithm 1 (read from the page image): input y_q, hyperparameters initialized to zero, E and M steps repeated until convergence or N_max; 'which runs at each AP independently'. p. 14: 'We fix the parameters for the proposed ConvBL algorithm as follows' (d = 10, step size 10^-2, 'maximum number of EM iterations Nmax = 100'). The paper has no training data, no neural network, and no deep unfolding; the baselines SBL [17], CPSBL [20], OMP [16], and the CRLB [37] (p. 14) are also untrained algorithms. The words 'learning' in the title and 'learning rate' (AdaGrad step size, p. 11) refer to hyperparameter estimation from each received pilot frame, not to a trained model, so the reviewer should confirm that SBL counts as an iterative algorithm under check 3. If it were counted as learned, the work would fall in area 4 (OTFS channel estimation in the delay-Doppler domain, with an IRS).
